source.title: Measured or Real? When Model-Derived Measurements Can Be Corrected or Compared

record.tranche_reason: Conceptually tests whether independently seeded networks share representations, using cross-seed feature reliability, Procrustes alignment, pairwise distances, and CKA rather than a scale sweep or the original studies’ methods.
record.gate_note: The study measures representation agreement across ResNet-18 seeds in Section 5 and Appendix H; these results are recorded below. Its model-size comparisons, language-model benchmark rankings, and item-difficulty reliability results do not measure representation convergence. It does not test whether agreement rises with model scale or capability.
record.test_reason: Section 5 and Appendix H directly measure representation agreement across independently trained ResNet-18 seeds, using held-out Procrustes alignment, distance correlations and CKA. These results test shared representations and metric dependence without testing convergence with scale.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the representation findings: raw per-dimension comparisons mostly reflect coordinate choice; held-out Procrustes alignment and basis-invariant measures reveal substantial cross-seed agreement. This is the conclusion of Section 5, rather than the whole paper's main conclusion, which concerns correcting noisy measurements and comparing models within prompt protocols.
record.recipe_differences: Uses cross-seed feature reliability, held-out orthogonal Procrustes alignment, pairwise-distance reliability, and CKA; it does not reproduce a scale-dependent convergence method.
record.method_sensitivity: Per-dimension reliability changes sharply with coordinate alignment. The paper also reports different agreement values across raw coordinates, aligned coordinates, pairwise distances, and CKA; aligned reliability is stable across the reference seed and fit share tested.
record.problems: The representation analysis covers only three seeds of ResNet-18 with the stated CIFAR training recipe. It does not vary scale, architecture, objective, training data, or modality. Embedding-result uncertainty intervals are not reported, and the feature matrices needed to regenerate the CIFAR-100 embedding results are not included in the released files.

untested.parts: No representation-alignment sweep over model scale or capability, or across architectures, objectives and training data.
No paired image-caption comparison between vision and language models.
Only three seeds per dataset, one architecture and penultimate features are examined; individual feature identities and other layers are not tested.
No downstream task or prediction loss after mapping, stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired images.
No comparison of interpretable neurons, SAE features or circuits.
No neighbour-count sweep, out-of-distribution evaluation, or controlled input-distribution change for a fixed trained model pair. The CIFAR studies use separately trained models.
No scale-related plateau or causal test of shared training data or objectives. Agreement indices below one alone do not establish that alignment stays far from complete.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the V3 limits_scope verdict based on raw coordinates: V3 explicitly permits different units and bases. Remove verdicts that treat untested mapping routes, downstream loss, causal explanations or scaling plateaus as scope failures. The study is not an original source for any version. Numerical values below one are not sufficient evidence for V7.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep, and no comparison across architectures, objectives, training data, or modalities.
Tests three seeds of ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100 and CIFAR-10; does not test different architectures, objectives, datasets as training regimes, or whether specific interpretable features recur.
Tests held-out orthogonal Procrustes alignment across seeds only. Does not test stitching layers, relative representations, mappings without paired data, or behavioral/task loss after mapping.
No interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits are compared.
Shows dependence on coordinate alignment and similarity measure, and reports results on CIFAR-100 and CIFAR-10. Does not test neighbour-count settings or out-of-distribution inputs.
Reports agreement below complete for several measures, but does not test a scale-related plateau or isolate shared training data/objectives as the cause of alignment.

rows.baseline: per-dimension reliability after held-out Procrustes alignment: 0.813
rows.note: The raw coordinate-wise result is near zero, in contrast to the aligned and basis-invariant measures. The paper interprets raw per-dimension reliability as mostly reflecting arbitrary coordinates.

Raw coordinate correlation alone cannot establish whether shared features or subspaces are absent; remove V3 and V7 links. The original partial state mistakes coordinate mismatch for incomplete representation convergence.
